documentation_evidence.observation: The curator describes the repository as a container for Windows event samples associated with specific attack and post-exploitation techniques and lists DFIR training and detection-use-case design as uses.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: This is a sample-and-technique organization statement, not an independent run, session, capture, or experiment registry.

documentation_evidence.observation: The folder is declared to host results from public automated EDR and MITRE ATT&CK testing tools, explicitly including Atomic Red Team and an EDR testing script.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: Tool, technique, or result identity cannot establish execution independence; the Atomic Red Team reference also creates source-generation and nuisance-overlap risk with the existing Atomic family.

documentation_evidence.observation: The document says this location will host malware execution traces combining multiple TTPs but supplies no run manifest or current group boundary.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: A future-intent statement cannot verify four current source-native executions.

documentation_evidence.observation: The document enumerates event IDs and telemetry indicators for several tunneling techniques but supplies no capture IDs, environment IDs, timestamps, or file-to-run mapping.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: Multiple events or telemetry providers for a technique may belong to one execution and cannot be counted independently.

documentation_evidence.observation: The documentation frames the material as datasets for analytics, ATT&CK tactic/technique visualization, and telemetry-provider analysis.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: ATT&CK and analytics metadata are supervision and organization aids, not lineage evidence.

documentation_evidence.observation: The document links to an external ANY.RUN task.
documentation_evidence.execution_group_implication: The repository contains mixed-origin material; external task identity is not a repository-wide independence guarantee.

execution_group_assessment.reason: The complete small-documentation surface at the pinned revision organizes samples by techniques, telemetry, tools, and external examples but never defines file membership for independently executed runs.

source_verification_grade.grade_interpretation: Primary GitHub metadata is authoritative for repository identity and proves the absence of a documented execution-group contract in all small documentation at the pinned revision. Strong artifact identity cannot compensate for missing scientific lineage.

reopen_conditions: The curator publishes a new immutable revision with a machine-readable manifest mapping files to at least four separately executed runs or captures.
The manifest records environment or host boundary, run/capture identity, time boundary, generation tool, file membership, and paired-view grouping without exposing labels to the model.
Atomic Red Team-derived and other externally sourced subsets are identified so curator, scenario, and nuisance overlap can be isolated before any split decision.
A new metadata-only review approves the new revision before any download.
forbidden_remediation: Count EVTX files, Git blobs, directories, tactics, techniques, providers, event IDs, or Git commits as independent execution groups.
Open EVTX payloads to infer runs when the curator has supplied no source-native grouping contract.
Use ATT&CK metadata, file paths, or technique labels as supervision or lineage.
Download first and decide provenance later.
next_action: Search metadata for a distinct executed endpoint or provenance family whose official artifact already exposes at least four source-native run or capture groups; do not download EVTX-ATTACK-SAMPLES at this revision.
